candidates.name: shoulder_peak_trim
candidates.reason: Trim expensive peaker block ends and split unit 6 around the afternoon trough; extend unit 5 through hour 23 to support the evening shutdown ramps. Local gradients suggest savings, subject to independent validation.

candidates.name: early_block_trim
candidates.reason: Combine shoulder and tail trims with removal of unit 3's initial one-hour block and a four-hour early outage of unit 5. Retain both large units because their attractive local gradients omit substantial cycling costs and capacity requirements.

candidates.name: cheaper_core_late_midmerit
candidates.reason: Keep cheaper unit 3 online and cycle unit 2 instead. Start unit 2 at hour 6 after its minimum outage, allowing unit 5's morning restart to move to hour 8 while retaining the shoulder, peaker and tail trims.

candidates.name: staggered_peak_start
candidates.reason: Use the cheaper core substitution and delayed unit 5 restart, but advance unit 7 to hour 9 and delay unit 8 to hour 11. This exchanges peaker block endpoints while retaining all three peakers through the midday peak and its shutdown shoulder.
